cues.en: Thank you to Squarespace for supporting PBS.
cues.zh: 感谢 Squarespace 对 PBS 的支持。

cues.en: Today, I'm going to tell you about the craziest proposal for an astrophysics mission that has a good chance of actually happening.
cues.zh: 今天，我要给大家讲一个最疯狂的天体物理学任务提案，它很有机会真的实现。

cues.en: Imagine a train of spacecraft sailing the sun's light to a magical point out there in space where the Sun's own gravity turns it into a gigantic lens.
cues.zh: 想象一列航天器乘着太阳光航行，驶向太空中一个神奇的点，在那里太阳自身的引力会把它变成一座巨大的透镜。

cues.en: What could such a solar system sized telescope see?
cues.zh: 这样一座太阳系大小的望远镜能看到什么？

cues.en: Pretty much anything, but definitely it could map the surfaces of alien worlds.
cues.zh: 几乎什么都能看到，但肯定能绘制外星世界的表面。

cues.en: Thanks to the Kepler mission, we now know that there are billions of extrasolar planets exoplanets
cues.zh: 多亏了 Kepler 任务，我们现在知道有数十亿颗太阳系外行星，也就是系外行星

cues.en: in our galaxy,
cues.zh: 在我们的银河系中，

cues.en: and we're learning a ton about them. For example, we figured out that there are something like 40,000,000,000
cues.zh: 而且我们正在大量了解它们。比如，我们发现大约有 400 亿

cues.en: or so Earth like planets,
cues.zh: 颗左右的类地行星，

cues.en: at least in terms of size and mass.
cues.zh: 至少从大小和质量来看是这样。

cues.en: Of course, if we wanna find life or actually visit these planets, it'd be nice to know a bit more than that. The James Webb Space Telescope is helping. It can detect different molecules in the atmospheres of exoplanets
cues.zh: 当然，如果我们想找到生命，或者真的去访问这些行星，知道得比这更多一点会更好。James Webb Space Telescope 正在帮忙。它能探测系外行星大气中的不同分子

cues.en: a bit larger than the Earth. JWST
cues.zh: 这些行星比地球稍大一些。JWST

cues.en: will even take images of some exoplanets,
cues.zh: 甚至会给一些系外行星拍照，

cues.en: but those images will never reveal anything more than a single dot in orbit around a star.
cues.zh: 但这些图像永远只能显示恒星轨道上的一个单点。

cues.en: If we find evidence for life, we're gonna wanna study it in detail,
cues.zh: 如果我们找到生命证据，我们会想详细研究它，

cues.en: ideally with images of the planetary surface.
cues.zh: 最好还有行星表面的图像。

cues.en: And if we ever wanna visit one of these exoplanets,
cues.zh: 如果我们真的想去访问其中一颗系外行星，

cues.en: it sure would be nice to know what lies at the end of such a many decade journey. But resolving the surface features of an exoplanet seems pretty impossible.
cues.zh: 知道这样一场长达数十年的旅程终点有什么，肯定很不错。但要分辨系外行星的表面特征似乎相当不可能。

cues.en: There's an absolute limit to the resolving power of any telescope, and it depends on size. Bigger is always better.
cues.zh: 任何望远镜的分辨能力都有绝对极限，而且取决于尺寸。越大总是越好。

cues.en: When light passes into a telescope,
cues.zh: 当光进入望远镜时，

cues.en: its wave nature interacts with the edge of the aperture of the telescope causing diffraction,
cues.zh: 它的波动性会与望远镜孔径的边缘相互作用，引起衍射，

cues.en: and that blurs the focus of the mirror or the lens.
cues.zh: 这会让镜面或透镜的焦点变模糊。

cues.en: The bigger the aperture, the smaller that blur.
cues.zh: 孔径越大，模糊越小。

cues.en: A telescope's diffraction limit is the best possible resolution it can achieve.
cues.zh: 望远镜的衍射极限是它能达到的最佳分辨率。

cues.en: If you try to create an image with anything smaller than this limit, then it will always get blurred out to the size of the diffraction limit. That's a problem because planets are pretty small when you're trying to see them from many light years away.
cues.zh: 如果你试图用小于这个极限的东西成像，它总是会被模糊到衍射极限的大小。这是个问题，因为当你从很多光年外看行星时，它们非常小。

cues.en: For example, to see a planet a 100 light years away as anything more than a dot, you'd need a telescope way bigger than New York City.
cues.zh: 例如，要把 100 光年外的一颗行星看得比一个点更多，你需要一座比纽约市大得多的望远镜。

cues.en: You might recall these pictures of the black holes in the m 87 galaxy and at the center of the Milky Way. These were taken by bringing together radio signals from telescopes all across the planet, effectively giving us a planet sized telescope with a tiny diffraction limit.
cues.zh: 你可能还记得 M87 星系和银河系中心黑洞的这些照片。它们是通过汇集全球各地望远镜的射电信号拍摄的，实际上给了我们一座行星大小、衍射极限极小的望远镜。

cues.en: We are not yet able to repeat this trick with visible light because this requires exact measurement of the arrival time and phase of the electromagnetic
cues.zh: 我们还不能对可见光重复这一招，因为这需要精确测量电磁

cues.en: wave, which gets harder the shorter the wavelength. But there is one way to take a direct image of an exoplanet
cues.zh: 波的到达时间和相位，而波长越短就越难。但有一种方法可以直接拍摄系外行星

cues.en: in visible light that could reveal its detailed surface features,
cues.zh: 用可见光，从而揭示其表面细节，

cues.en: and that's by sending a spaceship.
cues.zh: 那就是发射一艘飞船。

cues.en: Not to the planet. That would take way too long. In fact, it's by sending a spaceship in the opposite direction.
cues.zh: 不是去那颗行星。那会花太久。事实上，是向相反方向发射飞船。

cues.en: If you travel directly along the line connecting your favorite exoplanet
cues.zh: 如果你沿着连接你最喜欢的系外行星

cues.en: to the Sun but away from them both, you'll reach this spot where light rays from the exoplanet are bent inwards by the Sun's gravitational field to all come together.
cues.zh: 和太阳的直线，但朝远离两者的方向走，就会到达这个位置：来自系外行星的光线被太阳引力场向内弯折，全部汇聚到一起。

cues.en: Forget about a New York sized telescope.
cues.zh: 别提纽约那么大的望远镜了。

cues.en: At this spot, we have a star sized telescope.
cues.zh: 在这个位置，我们有一台恒星大小的望远镜。

cues.en: The result is an amplification of the brightness of the exoplanet by a factor of a trillion and a magnification
cues.zh: 结果是系外行星亮度被放大约一万亿倍，并且

cues.en: of the surface details by a factor of around a 100,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 表面细节约放大1000亿倍。

cues.en: The technical name for this location of incredible light converging power is the locus of focus hocus pocus,
cues.zh: 这个聚光能力惊人的位置，技术名称叫“焦点轨迹胡ocus pocus”，

cues.en: LFHP.
cues.zh: LFHP。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: That's just what it should be called. For some reason, the scientists went with SGLF,
cues.zh: 这才该是它的名字。可不知为何，科学家们用了 SGLF，

cues.en: solar gravitational lens focal region,
cues.zh: 太阳引力透镜焦区，

cues.en: a missed opportunity if you ask me. But if we can get a telescope into the
cues.zh: 要我说，这是错失良机。但如果我们能把望远镜送进

cues.en: SGLF,
cues.zh: SGLF，

cues.en: then we could start making detailed desk globes of alien worlds.
cues.zh: 那我们就能开始制作外星世界的精细桌面地球仪了。

cues.en: Let's talk about how we might actually achieve this because the plan is further along than you might think.
cues.zh: 我们来谈谈实际怎么做到，因为计划进展得比你想象得更远。

cues.en: Actually, you know what? Let's first review gravitational lensing.
cues.zh: 其实，你知道吗？我们先复习一下引力透镜。

cues.en: Einstein's general theory of relativity tells us that gravity is due to the curvature in the fabric of spacetime due to massive objects,
cues.zh: 爱因斯坦的广义相对论告诉我们，引力源于大质量物体造成的时空结构弯曲，

cues.en: but that curvature also bends the path of light.
cues.zh: 但这种弯曲也会弯折光的路径。

cues.en: You know what also bends light? Lenses.
cues.zh: 你知道还有什么能弯折光吗？透镜。

cues.en: So a gravitational field can also act like a lens, although admittedly a kind of crappy one.
cues.zh: 所以引力场也能像透镜一样起作用，虽然得承认是个很烂的透镜。

cues.en: Regular lenses are designed to bring light from the same point to a single focus point, allowing an image to be formed. Gravitational lenses produce highly distorted images like these stretched out galaxies seen through the gravitational field of a giant galaxy cluster.
cues.zh: 普通透镜的设计是把同一点的光汇聚到单一焦点，从而形成图像。引力透镜会产生高度扭曲的图像，比如透过巨大星系团引力场看到的这些被拉伸的星系。

cues.en: If the alignment is close enough, we can see an Einstein ring, like this galaxy being lensed by an intervening galaxy.
cues.zh: 如果对齐得足够近，我们就能看到爱因斯坦环，比如这个被中间星系透镜化的星系。

cues.en: The Sun also has a gravitational field that should create an Einstein ring of any distant object, including an exoplanet,
cues.zh: 太阳也有引力场，应该能为任何遥远天体，包括系外行星，形成爱因斯坦环，

cues.en: as long as you are watching from the correct location.
cues.zh: 只要你在正确的位置观察。

cues.en: So let's imagine we can find that location.
cues.zh: 那么，假设我们能找到那个位置。

cues.en: As I mentioned, you'd catch something like a trillion times more light from the exoplanet,
cues.zh: 正如我提到的，你会接收到来自系外行星约一万亿倍的光，

cues.en: making it possible to even see the thing in the first place,
cues.zh: 这首先让真正看到它成为可能，

cues.en: and the planet's surface area would be expanded by a factor of around a 100,000,000,000.
cues.zh: 而行星表面积会被放大约1000亿倍。

cues.en: If only it were possible to remove the distortion,
cues.zh: 要是能消除这种畸变就好了，

cues.en: we could map that surface in intricate detail.
cues.zh: 我们就能精细地绘制出那个表面。

cues.en: Well, it's not only possible, it's kind of easy.
cues.zh: 嗯，不仅可能，还挺容易。

cues.en: Gravitational lens images look messy. For example, here are some simulations of distant galaxies that have been lensed by a second galaxy much closer to us. The detailed structure is scrambled,
cues.zh: 引力透镜图像看起来很乱。比如，这些是遥远星系被一个离我们近得多的星系引力透镜化后的模拟图。精细结构被打乱了，

cues.en: but this is what you get when you try to reconstruct the original galaxy.
cues.zh: 但这就是你尝试重建原始星系时得到的结果。

cues.en: The results are remarkably close to the originals.
cues.zh: 结果和原始图像惊人地接近。

cues.en: We can go into the details of this process another time, and we should because it's actually a big part of my own research, but not today. Today, we're looking for aliens.
cues.zh: 这个过程的具体细节可以下次再讲，而且也该讲，因为它其实是我研究的重要部分，但不是今天。今天我们在找外星人。

cues.en: If it's possible to reconstruct the image from a messy galaxy lens, then it's completely straightforward to do it with the very clean, well understood gravitational
cues.zh: 如果可以从混乱的星系透镜中重建图像，那么用非常干净、已被充分理解的引力

cues.en: field of our Sun.
cues.zh: 场——太阳的引力场——来做就完全直接了。

cues.en: All we need to do is get our telescope to the right spot.
cues.zh: 我们只需要把望远镜送到正确的位置。

cues.en: Unfortunately, that spot is pretty far away, like 10 times the distance to Pluto or well over 500 times the Earth's orbital radius, around 550
cues.zh: 不幸的是，那个位置相当远，大约是到冥王星距离的10倍，或超过地球轨道半径的500倍，约550

cues.en: astronomical
cues.zh: 天文

cues.en: units or AUs
cues.zh: 单位，也就是 AU

cues.en: in astronomer speak.
cues.zh: 用天文学家的话说。

cues.en: For comparison, Voyager one is our most distant probe. It's been traveling for forty five years and is now around a 150 astronomical units from the Sun.
cues.zh: 作为对比，Voyager 1 是我们最远的探测器。它已经飞行了45年，现在距太阳约150个天文单位。

cues.en: To get a telescope to the SGLF,
cues.zh: 要把望远镜送到 SGLF，

cues.en: we'd want it to travel a little bit faster than that. So the researchers outlined two possibilities in their report to NASA. One is the flagship model in which a single craft with a one to two meter telescope
cues.zh: 我们希望它比那飞得稍快一些。于是研究者在给 NASA 的报告中提出了两种可能。一种是旗舰方案，用单个航天器搭载一台1到2米的望远镜

cues.en: is sent to do the work.
cues.zh: 去完成这项工作。

cues.en: The second is the string of pearls option in which many so called smallsats are sent in a long train, each riding on the light of the sun with a solar sail.
cues.zh: 第二种是“珍珠串”方案，把许多所谓的小卫星排成长队发送，每一颗都借助太阳帆，乘着太阳光前进。

cues.en: That second seems the preferred option,
cues.zh: 第二种似乎是更受青睐的方案，

cues.en: and, anyway, it's way cooler, so let's talk about that. Just as regular sails accelerate a ship by catching the momentum of the wind, solar sails catch the momentum of light, of photons from the sun.
cues.zh: 而且不管怎样，它酷多了，所以我们就聊这个。普通帆靠捕捉风的动量来加速船只，太阳帆则捕捉光的动量，也就是来自太阳的光子的动量。

cues.en: More traditional propulsion methods that carry their own fuel have hard constraints on payload size and acceleration period
cues.zh: 更传统的推进方式自带燃料，因此对载荷大小和加速时间有硬性限制

cues.en: because they're weighed down by their own fuel supply.
cues.zh: 因为它们被自己的燃料供应拖累了。

cues.en: But a solar sailing vessel doesn't carry fuel, making them great options for long range missions.
cues.zh: 但太阳帆航天器不携带燃料，这使它们成为远距离任务的绝佳选择。

cues.en: And this isn't even some sci fi far future tech. In 2010, the Japanese space agency sent the Ikaros probe to Venus using a 20 meter solar sail.
cues.zh: 这甚至不是科幻里的遥远未来技术。2010年，日本航天局用20米太阳帆把 Ikaros 探测器送往金星。

cues.en: And plenty more solar sail missions are in the design phase.
cues.zh: 还有更多太阳帆任务正处于设计阶段。

cues.en: But getting to 550
cues.zh: 但到达550

cues.en: astronomical
cues.zh: 天文

cues.en: units would be the most ambitious among these. In order to reach the destination
cues.zh: 单位，将是这些任务中最雄心勃勃的。为了抵达目的地

cues.en: during the working lifetime of at least some of the astronomers and engineers who actually witnessed the launch,
cues.zh: 至少要赶在一些亲眼见证发射的天文学家和工程师的职业生涯之内，

cues.en: we need a travel time of twenty five to thirty years.
cues.zh: 我们需要25到30年的飞行时间。

cues.en: So our spacecraft
cues.zh: 所以我们的航天器

cues.en: need an average speed of more than a 100 kilometers per second several times faster than Voyager.
cues.zh: 平均速度需要超过每秒 100 公里，比 Voyager 还要快上数倍。

cues.en: We'd want each craft to be very light,
cues.zh: 我们希望每个探测器都非常轻，

cues.en: ideally under a 100 kilograms.
cues.zh: 最好在 100 公斤以内。

cues.en: But with advanced modern materials, that seems possible.
cues.zh: 但借助现代先进材料，这似乎是可行的。

cues.en: Even with that mass, the solar sail would need to be enormous with more surface area than a football stadium.
cues.zh: 即使重量这么轻，太阳帆的面积依然要极其庞大，甚至超过一座足球场。

cues.en: Unfurling and then controlling such a giant sail is very difficult, so the scientists are proposing an advanced solar sail design called the sun vane,
cues.zh: 展开并控制如此巨大的帆非常困难，因此科学家提出了一种名为“日翼”（sun vane）的先进太阳帆设计，

cues.en: multiple controllable sail panels mounted along the narrow structure of the craft.
cues.zh: 也就是在航天器的狭长结构上安装多个可控的帆板。

cues.en: These sails would need to be made of some advanced low density metal alloy that's a, highly reflective,
cues.zh: 这些帆需要由某种先进的低密度金属合金制成，第一，反射率要极高；

cues.en: b, has a high melting temperature because as we'll see, it actually gets very close to the Sun, and c is only a few 100 atoms thick so it doesn't blow out our mass budget.
cues.zh: 第二，熔点要非常高，因为我们稍后会看到它会非常靠近太阳；第三，厚度只能有几百个原子，这样才不会超出质量预算。

cues.en: Solar sails experience more acceleration the closer they are to the Sun. To reach the speeds that we need, our spacecraft can't start their outward journey from the Earth. They need to get closer to the Sun first.
cues.zh: 太阳帆离太阳越近，获得的加速度就越大。为了达到所需的速度，我们的航天器不能从地球直接向外飞，而是要先向太阳靠近。

cues.en: This is how the proposed mission would play out.
cues.zh: 这项规划中的任务大概会这样展开。

cues.en: Our spacecraft
cues.zh: 我们的航天器

cues.en: start out by launching backwards
cues.zh: 首先会逆着

cues.en: compared to the Earth's orbital direction,
cues.zh: 地球的公转轨道方向发射，

cues.en: using sails to slow down and sort of tack inwards.
cues.zh: 利用太阳帆减速，并向内侧轨道变轨。

cues.en: They speed up rapidly plummeting towards the Sun, ideally at around a quarter of Mercury's orbital radius,
cues.zh: 它们在疾速冲向太阳的过程中大幅加速，理想位置是在水星轨道半径的大约四分之一处，

cues.en: assuming that we can make the thing sufficiently heat resistant.
cues.zh: 前提是我们能让它具备足够的耐热能力。

cues.en: Then the craft whip around the Sun and set their sails squarely against the intense up close solar radiation.
cues.zh: 接着，探测器绕过太阳，将太阳帆正对着近距离的强烈太阳辐射。

cues.en: That propels the craft on a trajectory that will take them out of the solar system and towards our first image of an exoplanet.
cues.zh: 这会推动探测器进入飞出太阳系的轨道，去拍摄我们首张系外行星的照片。

cues.en: Hitting the final destination is a feat of incredible astronavigation
cues.zh: 抵达最终目的地，将是一项令人难以置信的天体导航

cues.en: and maneuvering.
cues.zh: 和姿态机动壮举。

cues.en: The solar gravitational lens focal range is indeed a range. While a regular lens creates a focal point, the sun's gravitational field has a focal line starting at 550
cues.zh: 太阳引力透镜的聚焦范围确实是一个“区域”。普通透镜会形成一个焦点，而太阳的引力场则会形成一条焦线，它始于 550 个

cues.en: astronomical units, but extending indefinitely,
cues.zh: 天文单位，但会无限延伸，

cues.en: with the Einstein ring getting wider and more diffuse the further you go.
cues.zh: 越往深处走，爱因斯坦环就越宽、越发散。

cues.en: The column for an Earth sized exoplanet
cues.zh: 对于 100 光年外一颗地球大小的系外行星，其焦柱

cues.en: at a 100 light years is only 1.3
cues.zh: 直径仅仅只有

cues.en: kilometers across.
So this is really like threading a very, very tiny needle.
cues.zh: 所以这真的就像在穿一根极其微小的针眼。

cues.en: To hit the right spot, the craft will maneuver with tiny ion thrusters.
cues.zh: 为了精准命中目标区域，探测器将使用微型离子推进器来进行姿态机动。

cues.en: Once in the zone, the craft deploy its telescope.
cues.zh: 一旦进入该区域，探测器就会展开望远镜。

cues.en: One possibility is that multiple craft will assemble into a larger scope. It may even be possible to repurpose the light sail as a mirror if we wanna get really clever about this.
cues.zh: 一种可能性是多个探测器组装成一个更大的望远镜。如果更巧妙一点，甚至可能把光帆改装成一面反射镜。

cues.en: Once in place, our telescope just needs to point back at the Sun and take an image of the faint Einstein ring surrounding it. You might note an issue here.
cues.zh: 一旦就位，我们的望远镜只需调头对准太阳，拍下环绕其周围的微弱爱因斯坦环即可。你可能会注意到这里有个问题。

cues.en: The last thing you ever wanna do with a telescope is point it at the Sun. That's a great way to fry your camera, and good luck seeing anything next to the sun's intense glare.
cues.zh: 用望远镜最忌讳的就是把它对准太阳。这不仅很容易烧毁相机，而且在太阳刺眼的强光下，你根本什么都看不清。

cues.en: To deal with this, our telescope will use a coronagraph,
cues.zh: 为了解决这个问题，我们的望远镜会使用日冕仪，

cues.en: a giant circular mask that'll block the sun's light.
cues.zh: 这是一个巨大的圆形遮光罩，用来遮挡太阳光。

cues.en: From any one location within the focal column,
cues.zh: 在焦柱内的任意位置上，

cues.en: the newly deployed telescope will see an Einstein ring formed from a tiny patch on the surface of the planet, only 10 kilometers across.
cues.zh: 新部署的望远镜都能看到一个由行星表面极小区域形成的爱因斯坦环，这片区域跨度仅有10公里。

cues.en: In order to see the whole planet, it'll have to move around that focal column, mapping the surface one patch at a time.
cues.zh: 为了看清整颗行星，它必须在焦柱内移动，一块接一块地绘制出表面全貌。

cues.en: The ion thrusters come into play here also.
cues.zh: 离子推进器在这里也派上了用场。

cues.en: On top of this, the entire Einstein ring will be moving due to the motion of the exoplanet,
cues.zh: 此外，由于系外行星本身的公转，整个爱因斯坦环都会发生移动，

cues.en: but also due to the wobble of the Sun as it's tugged by the planets of our solar system.
cues.zh: 同时，太阳受到太阳系各行星的引力牵引而产生的晃动，也会导致它位移。

cues.en: Our telescope is going to execute this sort of shifting pirouette as it races away from the Sun, and that entire dance will have to be performed without any guidance from Earth due to the several day light travel time back to our planet.
cues.zh: 我们的望远镜在飞速远离太阳的同时，必须完成这种如同芭蕾旋转般的复杂机动；而且由于信号传回地球需要几天时间，整套动作都必须在没有地球引导的情况下自主完成。

cues.en: As you might have noticed, our spacecraft have no way of actually stopping, but that's okay.
cues.zh: 你可能已经注意到了，航天器根本没法停下来，但这没关系。

cues.en: The long focal line means that an Einstein ring will be visible for years of travel time,
cues.zh: 超长的焦线意味着在数年的飞行时间内，爱因斯坦环都将保持可见，

cues.en: slowly expanding outwards as we get further from the sun.
cues.zh: 并且随着我们远离太阳，它还会缓缓向外扩大。

cues.en: Remember that the scientists called this a string of pearls.
cues.zh: 还记得科学家们把这套方案称为“珍珠项链”吗。

cues.en: That first cluster of craft was the first pearl. Even if that group doesn't get this quite right, this data will help the next pearl learn, which should be following in about a year's time. And improved positioning and observing strategies will flow down the string of pearls.
cues.zh: 第一批航天器群就是第一颗珍珠。即使这批飞船表现不够完美，其数据也能为大约一年后跟进的下一颗珍珠提供参考。更优的定位与观测策略将在这条“珍珠项链”上一代代传递下去。

cues.en: Over time, the image that the train of spacecraft sends back to the Earth will get clearer and clearer. It should be possible to achieve a resolution of around 25 kilometers on the surface of an exoplanet a 100 light years away. We could map coastlines,
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，这支航天器梯队传回地球的图像会越来越清晰。它有望在100光年外的系外行星表面实现大约25公里的分辨率。我们可以绘制出海岸线，

cues.en: see islands and mountain ranges and lakes and ice caps,
cues.zh: 看清岛屿、山脉、湖泊和冰盖，

cues.en: and even vegetation,
cues.zh: 甚至还有植被，

cues.en: all of which we may be able to distinguish from their colors.
cues.zh: 所有这些我们或许都能通过颜色区分开来。

cues.en: And if we spot bright points of light on the planet's night side, well, that would be pretty compelling evidence of a technological civilization.
cues.zh: 如果我们在这颗行星的背光面发现明亮的光点，那将是存在科技文明的极有力证据。

cues.en: And over time, we'll see changes in all of this. That means we can remove cloud cover, track the change from day to night, see seasonal and tidal changes, and even changes due to the activity of life.
cues.zh: 而且随着时间推移，我们会看到所有这些细节的变化。这意味着我们可以滤除云层覆盖，追踪昼夜交替，观察季节和潮汐变化，甚至捕捉生命活动带来的变化。

cues.en: Every exoplanet that we want to image requires a new fleet. Now that sounds like a lot, but remember that we build dedicated spacecraft for each of our solar system's planets, usually more than one of them.
cues.zh: 我们想要成像的每一颗系外行星，都需要一支全新的舰队。听起来工程浩大，但别忘了，我们为太阳系内的每一颗行星都建造过专用航天器，而且通常还不止一艘。

cues.en: And these little smallsats are designed to be cheap,
cues.zh: 这些小型卫星的设计目标是廉价，

cues.en: so hopefully we'll eventually be able to do this for many exoplanets,
cues.zh: 所以希望最终我们能对许多系外行星做到这一点，

cues.en: and actually for distant galaxies and black holes and literally anything else for which we want extreme resolution imaging.
cues.zh: 而且实际上也能用于遥远星系、黑洞，以及任何我们想进行极高分辨率成像的目标。

cues.en: Maybe this all sounds a bit out there, but the technology involved is either existent or is in the development phase. Nothing seems like a deal breaker.
cues.zh: 也许这一切听起来有点天马行空，但相关技术要么已经存在，要么正处于开发阶段。目前看不出有什么致命障碍。

cues.en: There is no funded mission yet, but the scientists involved have been advanced to the phase three stage by the NIAC program.
cues.zh: 目前还没有获得资助的任务，但参与其中的科学家已被 NIAC 计划推进到第三阶段。

cues.en: The step after that, hopefully, is for the mission to be picked up by NASA.
cues.zh: 下一步希望是由 NASA 接手这个任务。

cues.en: We'll let you know how that goes,
cues.zh: 我们会告诉大家进展如何，

cues.en: but it's crazy to imagine that within our lifetimes,
cues.zh: 但想想就觉得很疯狂：在我们有生之年，

cues.en: we may have mapped in detail the surfaces of distant worlds
cues.zh: 我们也许就能详细绘制出遥远世界的地表，

cues.en: brought into focus by our own sun and its lens of curved spacetime.
cues.zh: 由我们自己的太阳及其弯曲时空透镜聚焦呈现。

cues.zh: AJ Mansfield 问 JWST

cues.zh: 是否也有一个计划，专门用来做那些附带的额外观测

cues.zh: 答案是有的。有一种特殊类型的提案，叫做所谓的并行

cues.en: observations.
cues.zh: 观测。

cues.en: Each primary observation
cues.zh: 每个主观测

cues.en: uses one of the telescope's instruments.
cues.zh: 会使用望远镜的一台仪器。

cues.en: Parallel observations just turn on one or more of the telescope's other detectors.
cues.zh: 平行观测只是开启望远镜的其他一个或多个探测器。

cues.en: These collect data a little off the field of the primary observation.
cues.zh: 它们会在主观测视场稍偏一点的地方收集数据。

cues.en: Sometimes these happen to land on useful objects, and sometimes they're more like blind surveys.
cues.zh: 有时它们恰好落在有用的天体上，有时更像是盲巡天。

cues.en: NASA is very careful to squeeze every bit of value out of the telescope that they can. Lyle Goodwin asks if the JWST
cues.zh: NASA 非常谨慎地尽可能榨取望远镜的每一点价值。Lyle Goodwin 问，JWST 是否

cues.en: completely supersedes Hubble.
cues.zh: 完全取代了哈勃。

cues.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题，也是我本该回应的问题。

cues.en: Actually, no. Hubble was most sensitive at visible and ultraviolet wavelengths,
cues.zh: 其实并没有。哈勃在可见光和紫外波段最灵敏，

cues.zh: 而 JWST

cues.en: is an infrared scope. These are very different instruments,
cues.zh: 是一台红外望远镜。它们是非常不同的仪器，

cues.en: and Hubble is still invaluable.
cues.zh: 而哈勃仍然极其宝贵。

cues.en: David Hawker asks how long did it take for the fine structure constant to drop to its minimum value of one over one thirty seven after the big bang? First, let me say that in the extremely early universe, the three quantum forces were coupled with a high joint interaction strength.
cues.zh: David Hawker 问，大爆炸后，精细结构常数降到其最小值 1/137 用了多长时间？首先我要说，在极早期宇宙中，三种量子力是以很高的联合相互作用强度耦合在一起的。

cues.en: However, it's really only meaningful to talk about the fine structure constant
cues.zh: 不过，真正有意义地讨论精细结构常数

cues.en: later on because
cues.zh: 要等到更晚的时候，因为

cues.en: it is the coupling constant of electromagnetism
cues.zh: 它是电磁相互作用的耦合常数

cues.en: which didn't exist at very early times.
cues.zh: 而电磁相互作用在极早期并不存在。

cues.en: About a trillionth of a second after the big bang, the e m force separated from the weak force, and then the fine structure constant was still within 10% of its current value and quickly approached one over one thirty seven as the universe cooled.
cues.zh: 大爆炸后约一万亿分之一秒，电磁力与弱力分离，当时精细结构常数仍在当前值的 10% 以内，并随着宇宙冷却迅速趋近于 1/137。

cues.en: By the time the first stars formed, it was essentially as it is today.
cues.zh: 到第一批恒星形成时，它基本上已经和今天一样了。

cues.en: Rader's law asks what exactly does energy of interaction mean.
cues.zh: Rader's law 问，相互作用能量到底指什么。

cues.en: Well, this is just the amount of energy available in a particle interaction for the creation of the interaction products.
cues.zh: 嗯，它只是粒子相互作用中可用于产生相互作用产物的能量。

cues.en: It comes from particle kinetic energy, photon energy, and even particle rest mass.
cues.zh: 它来自粒子动能、光子能量，甚至粒子静质量。

cues.en: The energy liberated in the interaction effectively raises the temperature of that tiny patch of space,
cues.zh: 相互作用中释放的能量实际上会升高那一小块空间的温度，

cues.en: and that can change the way the quantum fields behave,
cues.zh: 而这会改变量子场的表现方式，

cues.en: including raising the fine structure constant.
cues.zh: 包括提高精细结构常数。

cues.en: We routinely reach temperatures where the fine structure constant changes in our particle accelerators.
cues.zh: 在我们的粒子加速器中，经常能达到精细结构常数发生变化的温度。

cues.en: After all, we recreate the energies of the electroweak error when the fine structure constant isn't even relevant.
cues.zh: 毕竟，我们会重现电弱时期的能量，那时精细结构常数甚至都不重要。

cues.en: There aren't many natural places in the universe where this happens today.
cues.zh: 如今宇宙中能自然发生这种情况的地方并不多。

cues.en: Not in the centers of stars, not in accretion disks,
cues.zh: 不在恒星中心，也不在吸积盘，

cues.en: but perhaps in the cores of neutron stars we'd get there, I guess also in transient phenomena like supernovae or in cosmic ray collisions.
cues.zh: 但也许在中子星核心我们能达到，我猜在超新星这类瞬变现象或宇宙线碰撞中也可以。

cues.en: Death waits for no one asks
cues.zh: 死亡从不等人发问

cues.en: if the fine structure constant wasn't constant like during the big bang, wouldn't the relationship between the other constants also be different during that time?
cues.zh: 如果精细结构常数并不恒定，就像大爆炸期间那样，那当时其他常数之间的关系不也会不同吗？

cues.en: Well, yes.
cues.zh: 嗯，是的。

cues.en: The fine structure constant is defined as the electron charge squared
cues.zh: 精细结构常数定义为电子电荷的平方

cues.en: divided by four pi times the vacuum permittivity
cues.zh: 除以 4π 乘以真空介电常数

cues.en: times the Planck constant times the speed of light.
cues.zh: 再乘以普朗克常数和光速。

cues.en: If the fine structure constant was different,
cues.zh: 如果精细结构常数不同，

cues.en: then one or more of these other constants would have to be different.
cues.zh: 那么这些其他常数中至少有一个必须不同。

cues.en: Could the Planck constant or the speed of light change? Well, in principle, maybe. But the most natural thing is to change the ratio of the electric charge squared to the vacuum permittivity.
cues.zh: 普朗克常数或光速会变吗？原则上也许可能。但最自然的做法是改变电子电荷平方与真空介电常数的比值。

cues.en: Remember that the fine structure constant represents the strength of electromagnetism,
cues.zh: 记住，精细结构常数代表电磁力的强度，

cues.en: and the classical equation for the electrostatic force, Coulomb's law, has charge squared over permittivity.
cues.zh: 而静电力的经典方程，即库仑定律，是电荷平方除以介电常数。

cues.en: So changing these changes the strength of the force, which is the right effect.
cues.zh: 所以改变这些就会改变力的大小，这正是想要的效果。

cues.en: Michael Niles speculates that the fine structure constant was set when the four d experimentalists
cues.zh: Michael Niles 推测，精细结构常数是在四维实验物理学家们

cues.en: coding our universe meant to type Leet for the seed phrase and made a typo.
cues.zh: 编写我们宇宙时，本想为种子短语输入 Leet，却打错了字。

cues.en: Look. If this is true, then there should be other Leet speak messages in the other constants.
cues.zh: 听着。如果这是真的，那其他常数里应该还有别的 Leet 语信息。

cues.en: And I looked
cues.zh: 于是我去找

cues.en: extensively
cues.zh: 广泛地找

cues.en: and didn't find anything.
cues.zh: 什么也没找到。

cues.en: But then I realized that pi is an irrational number with infinite digits, which means if you look far enough it says lol noobs
cues.zh: 但后来我意识到，π 是无理数，有无穷多位，这意味着只要看得足够远，它就会说“lol noobs”

cues.en: infinite times.
cues.zh: 无限次。
